clauses.reason: Three scopes carry one amendment, divided by the dossier into the amendment instruction and its two items (offsets 817-1708, 1709-1814 and 1815-2242 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10681.txt, 21 FR 8129): signed 1956-10-22; under sections 204 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, amends section 4 of Executive Order 10152 (incentive pay for hazardous duty) by adding a new subsection (c) stating minimum flight requirements for members of Reserve components who perform both active-duty and inactive-duty training in the same calendar month and may qualify for incentive pay under both sections. The held OCR of this order has damaged words in the lead and in the two items (for example a damaged first word of item (1) and a damaged word in item (2)), but the structure and the references to subdivision (4) of subsections (a) and (b) are legible; EO 11157 section 104(c), at offsets 6050-6500 of its held text, restates the same rule in legible form. No sunset or condition ends the added subsection. Later orders that amended the parent EO 10152 did not amend section 4: EO 10739 adds a subsection to section 9, and EO 11120 (signed 1963-10-02, effective as of 1963-10-01) amends sections 6, 8(a), 9, 10, 12 and 13 (held text offsets 1170-3700) and does not name section 4. This scope is the operative lead: the amendment instruction and the heading and opening of new subsection (c) (offsets 817-1708).

research_rationale:
EO 10681 is a strike-and-insert or addition amendment of a pay-and-allowance regulation order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling (owner ruling 2026-10-21, option B) its clauses continue, as amended, until the parent order ends. The first held end is the express revocation by EO 11157 section 502 (signed 1964-06-22, no effective-date wording), which names this order and its parent. The 1962 title 37 recodification is disclosed as an unnamed earlier candidate that I read as restating without substantive change (Public Law 87-649 section 12). Searches: no U.S. Code or eCFR hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists the chain events recorded in the dossier.
